In [[mathematics]], '''Fujita's conjecture''' is a problem in the theories of [[algebraic geometry]] and [[complex manifold]]s. It is named after Takao Fujita, who formulated it in 1985.

==Statement==
In complex geometry, the conjecture states that for a [[Positive_form#Positive_line_bundles|positive]] [[holomorphic line bundle]] <math>L</math>  on a [[compact space|compact]] complex manifold <math>M</math>, the line bundle <math>K_M \otimes L^{\otimes m}</math> (where <math>K_M</math> is a [[Canonical bundle|canonical line bundle]] of <math>M</math>) is 
* [[spanned by sections]] when  <math>m\geq n+1</math>;
* [[very ample]] when <math>m\geq n+2</math>,

where <math>n</math> is the [[complex dimension]] of <math>M</math>.

Note that for large <math>m</math> the line bundle <math>K_M \otimes L^{\otimes m}</math> is very ample by the standard [[Serre's vanishing theorem]] (and its complex analytic variant). The Fujita conjecture provides an explicit bound on <math>m</math>, which is optimal for [[projective space]]s.

==Known cases==
For surfaces the Fujita conjecture follows from [[Reider's theorem]]. For three-dimensional algebraic varieties, Ein and Lazarsfeld in 1993 proved the first part of the Fujita conjecture, i.e. that <math>m\geq 4</math> implies global generation.
